open_points.subject: EXECUTION_STATUS_CONCLUSIONS
open_points.text: “the conclusion each NodeExecution status gives (A13 rules 5 and 7) ... a table here keyed by the enumeration, total over its members, whose cells name members”
open_points.question: Which enumeration supplies the table’s cell values, and what value corresponds to every NodeExecution status? No node-conclusion enumeration or complete mapping is defined in models.
options: Add a closed NodeConclusion enumeration and give every table entry
Use NodeExecutionStatus members as the values
Use existing run and waiting statuses as values, requiring a structured cell
open_points.default_guess: Introduce a NodeConclusion enumeration containing succeeded, failed, skipped_by_guard, waiting, refused and dynamic_effect_outcome, then map every NodeExecution status explicitly.

open_points.subject: outcome_unknown conclusion
open_points.text: “the conclusion each NodeExecution status gives ... a table here keyed by the enumeration, total over its members”
open_points.question: What single table value represents `outcome_unknown`, whose actual conclusion can be waiting, succeeded, failed with `applied_outputs_unknown`, or ready for another attempt depending on the EffectAttempt resolution and whether the binding has outputs?
options: The table gives only the unresolved preliminary conclusion and `effects.operation_element_conclusion` overrides it
Key the correspondence by status plus EffectAttempt state and binding-output presence
Use a special table member meaning that `effects` must determine the conclusion
open_points.default_guess: Use a special dynamic member and let `effects.operation_element_conclusion` determine the resolved conclusion before run_graph applies node effects.

open_points.subject: NODE_CONCLUSION_EFFECTS
open_points.text: “what each node conclusion means for the run and for its dependants (A13 rules 5 and 7) ... a table here keyed by the enumeration, total over its members, whose cells name members”
open_points.question: What is the key enumeration, what columns does each cell contain, and what are the exact entries for success, guard skip, failure, wait, and owner refusal? In particular, the text does not say how ‘no forced dependant conclusion’ or ‘run remains unfinished’ is represented while requiring cells to name enumeration members.
options: Each row is a pair of run effect and dependant effect, with dedicated enumerations including neutral members
Use two separate total tables, one for run effects and one for dependant effects
Map directly to optional RunStatus and NodeExecutionStatus members
open_points.default_guess: Use a row with two dedicated enum-valued fields, `run_effect` and `dependant_effect`, each having an explicit neutral member, and list every mapping.

open_points.subject: HTTP_METHOD_BODIES
open_points.text: “whether an HTTP method carries a body (A09 rule 2) ... a table here keyed by the enumeration, total over its members, whose cells name members”
open_points.question: What do the cells of HTTP_METHOD_BODIES contain? A09 fixes a yes/no property, but no body-policy enumeration exists whose members the cells could name.
options: Boolean cells: GET and DELETE false; POST, PUT and PATCH true
Add a BodyPolicy enumeration such as no_body/body and use its members
Store sets of methods instead of the stated total keyed table
open_points.default_guess: Use Boolean cells with GET and DELETE false and POST, PUT and PATCH true, treating the ‘cells name members’ statement as inapplicable to this table.
